description.narrative: Målet med Moldova Innovation och entreprenörskap är att bidra till ekonomisk utveckling och arbetstillfällen genom att utveckla landets system för innovation och entreprenörskap, kvinnligt företagande och startups.

The overall aim of the Innovate Moldova programme is to foster sustainable economic growth and job creation through the development of innovation ecosystem and entrepreneurship, including women entrepreneurs and startups

The overall aim of the Innovate Moldova programme is to foster sustainable economic growth through the development of innovation ecosystem and entrepreneurship through three objectives:
1. Building a stronger Innovation Ecosystem through enhanced collaboration among business support organisations, accelerators and knowledge institutions,
2. Developing a future-ready workforce by equipping individuals, especially youth and women, with the skills necessary for success in the digital and STEAM-driven job market (STEAM = Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Math),
3. Strengthening Private Sector Competitiveness by supporting businesses in improving their capabilities and access to EU and global markets, ensuring they are well-positioned for international growth and innovation.

The Innovate Moldova Programme was set up in spring 2025 to keep the momentum in the Swedish support to innovation-driven economic growth and job creation in Moldova, after the US unilaterally in February 2025 decided to close the joint cooperation through the Future Technologies Activity Programme (FTA). The core-team of the FTA programme was transferred to the FAM - foundation.
Sida considers that the Innovate Moldova team has managed the transition well and been able to continue the operations in line with the Swedish reform cooperation strategy for inclusive economic development in Moldova.
Innovate Moldova has established a monitoring and evaluation system with a detailed set of indicators to measure performance against the set objectives. During the eight month in 2025, 81 of the indicators were met or exceeded targets, 28 were not met and 25 were transferred to 2026.
Innovate Moldova has set ambitious targets when it comes to resource mobilisation / leverage of funds. During 2025, for every 1 SEK invested by the project 6.5 SEK was mobilised (out of 1,5 M Euro invested by the project; 5,1 M Euro from private sector, 1,6 M Euro from Government and 3,2 M Euro from other donors).
As this was the first eight months of implementation it is too early yet for any outcome results and the results are at this stage mostly on activity and output levels. Some examples:
Objective 1: Building a stronger innovation system
The Innovate Moldova team signed collaboration agreement with Moldovan partners that together form the Moldova innovation and entrepreneurship eco- system: 12 innovation centres, 6 business associations, 3 universities, Moldova Virtual Innovation and Technology Park, and MoUs with Ministry of Economy and Research, Ministry of Culture, Ministry of Education and Moldovan Investment Agency.
In terms of EU-alignment: Launched an ESG reporting toolkit for SMEs (ESG = Environmental and Social Governance); Dialogue led by the textile manufacturers branch organisation (APIUS) on prepare an integrated platform for core-business activities (ERP) and Eco-design.
Objective 2: Developing a future-ready, inclusive workforce
Agreements and MoUs were signed to continue som of the flagships programme initiated during FTA, such as the: Future Classroom Labs engaging approximately 20,000 students and 200 teachers across the country; Future Professions 600 students enrolled and 200 graduated in 2025 in animation, game-design and multimedia at four universities and 10 youth led startups supported through the Future Creatives initiative; Cybersecurity training at Cybercor of 100 public agency staff and 300 university students out of which 30% women, through the GLIA women Impact Hub, 500 girls (students) and 100 women professionals took part in the financial-literacy programme.
Objective 3: Strengthening private-sector competitiveness and export readiness
Through various initiatives about 100 SMEs received support to improve their ability to trade with EU and access to global markets: through the BRIDGE reimbursable grant scheme (joint collaboration with Moldova Investment Agency, UMAEF and EU4Innovation): 30 start-ups graduated from the business accelerator Technovator and Startup Moldova; APIUS Smart factory initiative supported 8 apparel manufacturers to obtain ISO 9001/14001/45001 certification; AIM (the association of SMEs) mentored 50 SMEs on e-commerce and market place logistics.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
